# Ajakalāpaka Sutta (Ud 1.7 (PTS Ud 4))

**ID:** Ud 1.7 (PTS Ud 4)

**Title (Pali):** Ajakalāpaka Sutta

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ajakalāpaka Sutta* (Ud 1.7, PTS Ud 4) is the seventh discourse of the first chapter (Bodhivagga) of the *Udāna*. Set at the Ajakalāpaka Shrine in Pāvā, the narrative recounts an episode where the Buddha is seated out in the open air during a dark night while light rain is falling [Masefield 1997]. Intending to provoke fear, stupefaction, and horripilation in the Buddha, the resident *yakkha* Ajakalāpaka approaches him, eliciting an inspired utterance in which the Buddha declares that an awakened person who has penetrated the truth and eradicated defilements has gone beyond all fear [Masefield 1997].

The sutta and its titular spirit-deity are cited in scholarly studies of early Buddhist popular religion and iconography; Robert DeCaroli discusses Ajakalāpaka as an example of a local spirit associated with a specific shrine who also finds mention in monument inscriptions such as those at Bhārhut [DeCaroli 2004], and Étienne Lamotte examined the figure in a dedicated comparative study of the *yakṣas* Ajakalāpaka and Bakkula [Lamotte 1987].
